card.summary: The Railway Safety Act of 2026 establishes new safety requirements for trains carrying hazardous materials, mandates minimum freight train crew sizes, updates inspection and defect detection rules, increases civil penalties for rail safety violations, and provides funding for emergency response and preparedness grants.
card.title: Railway Safety Act of 2026

selection.reason: Impact scored and summarised by Gemini.

summary: H.R. 7748, the Railway Safety Act of 2026, aims to enhance safety requirements for trains transporting hazardous materials and improve overall rail safety. The bill mandates safety standards for high-hazard trains, establishes minimum crew sizes for freight trains, requires advanced defect detection systems and enhanced track and equipment inspections, increases penalties for rail safety violations, and provides grants and emergency response programs for hazardous materials preparedness.

affected_groups.effect: Must comply with new speed limits, crew size minimums, real-time electronic train consist reporting, enhanced inspection schedules, and new defect detection networks, and face higher penalties for safety violations.
affected_groups.group: Class I and other railroad carriers

affected_groups.effect: Guaranteed a 2-person crew standard on most freight trains, subject to alcohol and drug testing if performing inspections, and protected against time limits being imposed on safety inspections.

Receive better hazard information, virtual and in-person training options, grant funding for personal protective equipment and exercises, and access to an emergency response assistance fund for significant hazardous materials incidents.
affected_groups.group: State, local, and Tribal emergency responders

affected_groups.effect: Subject to phase-out schedules for older tank car models and increased research and development funding and regulations regarding safer tank car features.

key_provisions: Establishes federal safety requirements and speed limits for high-hazard trains, including lower speed limits in high-threat urban areas and real-time electronic train consist information shared with emergency responders and fusion centers.
Mandates a minimum 2-person freight train crew size consisting of a conductor and a locomotive engineer for Class I railroads, with specific exceptions.

Requires Class I railroads to implement risk-based defect detector network plans, including specific spacing for hot bearing detectors, and authorizes grants to assist commuter railroads with compliance.
Requires Class I railroads to use designated inspectors for pre-departure freight car inspections and creates minimum requirements for periodic freight car inspections and locomotive inspections.
Increases civil penalties for rail safety violations, raising maximum penalties significantly and allowing higher penalties for violations resulting in severe harm or showing conscious disregard.
Phases out older tank cars used for transporting Class 3 flammable liquids by December 31, 2027, unless they meet newer specifications.

Creates an emergency response assistance program within the Department of Transportation to provide immediate financial assistance and reimbursements to communities responding to significant hazardous materials transportation incidents.
missing_information: Exact total costs and appropriations needed for all new federal programs beyond specified amounts like $25 million for research grants and $5 million for tank car research.
